Osmium.name: Osmium
Osmium.description: Hard, brittle, bluish metal. Popular in alloys. When paired with Iridium, it forms the densest metal known to man. Unfortunately, this density makes it impractical to incorporate it into ships.

Iridium.name: Iridium
Iridium.description: Iridium is an extremely hard, brittle, silvery metal. Popular in allows. When combined with Osmium, it forms the densest metal known to man, which makes it difficult and unweidly in ship design.

Palladium.name: Palladium
Palladium.description: Lustrous, silvery metal. Its bright sheen makes it a popular choice for plating in luxury applications.

Gallium.name: Gallium
Gallium.description: A soft, silvery metal with a very low melting point. Such a low melting point that it will become soft in your hand, which isn't very practical.

Plutonium.name: Plutonium
Plutonium.description: Plutonium is a silvery grey metal that tarnishes quickly. It is also extremely radioactive, and the most common choice for fission reactors in ships and power stations. The most reactive isotope, Plutonium-239, is quite useful for weapons, so all Plutonium is heavily regulated all human governments. Being caught with unregistered Plutonium samples can result in a hefty fine, or jail time. Small pieces of Plutonium can be found in scrap metal drifting throughout space as the leftovers of reactors, batteries, and weapons.

Manganite.name: Manganite
Manganite.description: Manganite is a mineral composed mostly of manganese. It isn't terribly useful except as an ore. In prehistoric times, it was used as a dye, pigment, and even a fire starter, but those days are past.

Scandium.name: Scandium
Scandium.description: Scandium is a silvery metal that is useful in many alloys used in shipbuilding. It is most popularly used with Aluminum.

Vanadium.name: Vanadium
Vanadium.description: Vanadium is useful in alloys and batteries. Alloys containing vanadium date back long before human spaceflight in luxury applications, surgical tools, and the old turbine engines of The Jet Age. Modern fusion reactors are heavily dependent on Vanadium as a superconductor, since it is necessary to form the electromagnetic tauruses where fusion occurs.

Cobalt.name: Cobalt
Cobalt.description: Cobalt is an important, but very common metal. It is used in batteries for the most part, but its value is diminished by its plenty.

Coal.name: Coal
Coal.description: Coal is a form of pure Carbon that is formed deep in the crusts of planets from the decay of Carbon-based plants and animals. It is common on planets, but rare in space, where it is only present because of planetary collisions and disasters.

Diamond.name: Diamond
Diamond.description: Another form of pure Carbon, formed deep in the crusts of seismically active planets. It is valuable both as the hardest mineral short of Yottrite, and as a beautiful gemstone.

Lithium.name: Lithium
Lithium.description: Lithium is important as a component of hyperspace fuel, but it is also the third-most common element in the galaxy, so it doesn't go for much.

Sulfur.name: Sulfur
Sulfur.description: Sulfur is an abundant nonmetallic element that has a strong smell. It is useful in making conventional munitions and propellants, and noxious vapors too.

Nickel.name: Nickel
Nickel.description: Nickel is used in batteries and metal alloys. It is also a necessary component in atomic engines.

Beryllium.name: Beryllium
Beryllium.description: Beyllium is a hard and brittle material, it is useful in various scientific applications and it is valuable because of its rarity.

Glass.name: Glass
Glass.description: Glass is formed by the heat of your weapons against Silicon powder in asteroids. That said, its basically useless unless it is manufactured in a pure form. Small amounts are present in scrap and junk floating throughout space.

Quartz.name: Quartz
Quartz.description: Quartz is a form of Silicon Dioxide that forms pretty hexagonal crystals. When charged pizzoelectrically, Quartz oscilates in a regular manner and it is used in clocks as a cheaper alternative to Rubidium and Caesium.

Basalt.name: Basalt
Basalt.description: Basalt is igneous rock blasted off of planets and asteroids when they interact. It is basically useless and uninteresting.

Granite.name: Granite
Granite.description: Granite is mostly composed of Silicon, and its beautiful appearance makes it popular for use in buildings on planets, but it is too heavy and brittle to be of much use in a spaceship.

Hematite.name: Hematite
Hematite.description: Hematite is a variant of Iron Oxide. It is valuable as Iron ore and a red pigment.

Magnetite.name: Magnetite
Magnetite.description: Magnetite is another variant of Iron Oxide. It is a simple and ferromagnetic mineral abundant in most parts of the galaxy.

Steel.name: Steel
Steel.description: Steel is comprised of a variety of different Iron alloys. Steel in space comes from the remains of spaceships that have degraded in space or have been destroyed in combat.

Brass.name: Brass
Brass.description: Brass is an alloy of copper and tin, its heat and electrical conductivity make it popular in ship components. Essentially all of the brass in space comes from destroyed starships, but it does occur naturally every now and then.

Obsidian.name: Obsidian
Obsidian.description: Obsidian is igneous glass that becomes very sharp when broken. Scalpels and other instruments of surgery can be fashioned from obsidian.

Schist.name: Schist
Schist.description: Schist is a completely uninteresting rock.

Feldspar.name: Feldspar
Feldspar.description: Feldspar rock is a mix of a variety of crystals and silicates. It is essentially useless in the modern world.

Upgraded Mining Laser.name: Upgraded Mining Laser
Upgraded Mining Laser.description: This is a heavily modified and upgraded variant of the trusty Mining Laser. It includes improved optics that improve accuracy and range, higher strength components, and light frequencies adapted to decomposing rock instead of vaporizing it. The new design makes it even less effective against shields than before, and much more epxensive to build.
